subtitle: A secret war plan hits page one
photoCredit: Albert C. Wedemeyer, author of the Rainbow Five plan, about 1942. U.S. Army Signal Corps photo 196260, public domain.
body:
Readers in Chicago open their paper this morning to a banner headline: "F.D.R.'S WAR PLANS!"

Chicago Tribune reporter Chesly Manly has a copy of Rainbow Five, the top secret plan the Army and Navy drew up to fight Germany. It calls for an army of ten million men, with five million sent overseas to invade Europe. The Washington Times Herald prints it too.

Inside the War Department, officers are stunned. The man who wrote the plan, Major Albert Wedemeyer, finds himself under suspicion as investigators hunt for the leak. The country is still at peace, and the story sets off a political storm.
